cues.caption: Hello, champ! Ready for Chapter 4?
cues.text: Hello, champ! Welcome back to Mentr Learn. Are you ready for Chapter four?

cues.caption: Ch 1: Computers · Ch 2: Binary · Ch 3: Devices
cues.text: So far, we learned what a computer is, how it thinks in ones and zeros, and the devices that bring information in and out.

cues.caption: Chapter 4 · How Websites Talk to Each Other
cues.text: Today's lesson is: How Websites Talk to Each Other.

cues.caption: Say with me: Websites talk to each other!
cues.text: Say it with me… Websites… talk… to each other!

cues.caption: The secret trip of a website
cues.text: By the end, you will know the secret trip a website takes to reach your screen.

cues.caption: Where does the cartoon come from?
cues.text: When you open a cartoon on a tablet, where does that cartoon come from?

cues.caption: Is it hiding inside your tablet? Think!
cues.text: Is it hiding inside your tablet? Pause and think.

cues.caption: It comes from another computer, far away!
cues.text: Here is the surprise. Most of it is not inside your tablet at all. It comes from another computer, far, far away!

cues.caption: Internet = millions of computers joined together
cues.text: That is the internet. The internet is not one big box. It is millions of computers, all joined together, all over the world.

cues.caption: ASKERS: your tablet, phone, laptop
cues.text: Some computers ask for things — like your tablet, phone, or laptop. Let's call them askers.

cues.caption: ANSWERERS: servers keep websites ready
cues.text: Other computers answer. They keep websites and videos ready, all day and all night. They are called servers.

cues.caption: Internet = asking and answering
cues.text: So the internet is many computers asking and answering, again and again.

cues.caption: Say: Ask… and answer!
cues.text: Say it with me: Ask… and answer!

cues.caption: A website is like a shop
cues.text: Now, what is a website? A website is like a shop on the internet.

cues.caption: Your home has an address
cues.text: Think of your home. It has an address, so a friend or a delivery person can find it.

cues.caption: A website's address = URL
cues.text: Every website also has an address. It is called a URL. You type it at the top of the screen.

cues.caption: mentr.com → the name + the ending
cues.text: For example, mentr dot com. The name tells us which shop, and dot com is like the end of the address.

cues.caption: Say: URL = website address
cues.text: Say it with me: U… R… L… means website address!

cues.caption: Questions travel on invisible roads
cues.text: But how does your question travel so far? On roads! Not real roads — invisible ones.

cues.caption: Wi-Fi: a road from the router
cues.text: Wi-Fi is a road at home or at school. It comes from a small box called a router.

cues.caption: Mobile data: a road through towers
cues.text: Mobile data is another road. It travels through big towers, so it works even outside your home.

cues.caption: Roads only CARRY questions and answers
cues.text: Remember: roads do not make the website. They just carry the question, and the answer.

cues.caption: Follow one trip, step by step
cues.text: Now let's follow one full trip, step by step.

cues.caption: Step 1: You type the address
cues.text: Step one: you type the address, mentr dot com, and press enter.

cues.caption: Step 2: Your device asks — a request
cues.text: Step two: your device sends a message on the road: Please send me this page! This message is called a request.

cues.caption: Step 3: The server finds the page
cues.text: Step three: the server gets the request, and finds the page.

cues.caption: Step 4: The server sends it back
cues.text: Step four: the server sends the page back, on the road, to your device.

cues.caption: Step 5: The page appears!
cues.text: Step five: the page appears on your screen. Ta-da!

cues.caption: All in less than 1 second!
cues.text: And guess what? This whole trip usually takes less than one second!

cues.caption: Game: fix the mixed-up steps
cues.text: Game time! Here are three steps, all mixed up.

cues.caption: Put them in order — think!
cues.text: Page appears. Type address. Device asks. Which comes first, second, and third? Think!

cues.caption: Type address → Device asks → Page appears
cues.text: First, type the address. Second, your device asks. Third, the page appears. Well done!

cues.caption: Watching a cartoon online
cues.text: One more real-life example. When you watch a cartoon online…

cues.caption: Ask for the next piece… answer… again!
cues.text: …your tablet does not get the whole cartoon at once. It keeps asking for the next little piece, and the server keeps answering.

cues.caption: Slow road → spinning circle (buffering)
cues.text: If the road is slow, the pieces come late. That is why a video sometimes stops and shows a spinning circle!

cues.caption: Practice check
cues.text: Practice check — the same kind of question you will see in the quiz.

cues.caption: First: page appears, or device asks?
cues.text: When you open a website, what happens first? The page appears, or your device asks for it?

cues.caption: Hint: can a server answer before you ask?
cues.text: Think: can a server send a page before anyone asks for it?

cues.caption: Answer: your device ASKS first
cues.text: Right! Your device asks first. Then the page appears.

cues.caption: Internet = computers asking & answering
cues.text: Let's lock it in. The internet is many computers, asking and answering.

cues.caption: Website = shop · Address = URL
cues.text: A website is like a shop, and its address is called a URL.

cues.caption: Wi-Fi & mobile data = roads
cues.text: Wi-Fi and mobile data are roads that carry the questions and answers.

cues.caption: Type → Ask → Page appears
cues.text: And the trip: type the address, your device asks, the page appears.

cues.caption: Chapter 4 complete!
cues.text: Chapter four done! Now you know how websites talk. Superb work, champ!

cues.text: Next, a short quiz to practise. Tap Finish when you are ready. See you there, champ!
